system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

exchanges.user:
ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer-side review:** The Seller’s “[STANDARD]”, “FINAL” and “already agreed” labels are not evidence of Buyer approval. The positions below are proposed Buyer negotiating targets—not assertions of market practice. The underlying SPA and DD documents must be checked; the Seller’s summaries are not independent verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | 20% of price: **AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery for general warranty breaches, separate from higher-protection categories. | **Counter at 100% of price (AUD 24m)**, with any reduction commercially negotiated after diligence; a 20% cap may leave substantial acquisition risk with Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000**; **AUD 250,000 deductible basket**, recovering only the excess. | Lower thresholds, related-claim aggregation and a tipping basket. | **Propose AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 100,000 tipping basket**, recovering qualifying claims from the first dollar once crossed; the draft combines substantial claim exclusion with an uninsured deductible. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notice within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | At least **24 months** for general warranties, with separate category-specific periods. | **Counter at 24 months**, preserving timely notified claims until resolved and allowing reasonable notice detail; 18 months may not expose problems across two annual reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title share the general cap and time limit. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership, valid issuance, transfer and freedom from encumbrances. | **Require a separate 100%-of-price cap, no thresholds and a six-year contractual claim period**, subject to execution form and applicable law; Buyer must have meaningful recourse if it does not acquire the promised shares. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express preservation of fraud remedies and rights that cannot lawfully be excluded. | **Carve fraud and fraudulent misrepresentation out of caps, thresholds, contractual time bars, disclosure/knowledge defences and remedy/reliance restrictions**, with attribution expressly addressed; the Seller must not contractually shelter fraudulent conduct. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, referenced material, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with enough detail to identify their nature and scope, against identifiable warranties. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure; require specific disclosures and a frozen, indexed disclosure record**, with any general exceptions narrowly negotiated; mere document availability should not transfer unidentified risks. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | Bars claims for Buyer/adviser knowledge, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No constructive knowledge or adviser-wide imputation; preferably no knowledge bar. | **Delete; if unavoidable, restrict to actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer deal leads, without enquiry duties**, excluding protected claim categories; “discoverable” would undermine the warranty bargain. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; condition satisfied on delivery of written consent, although final consent and satisfaction of associated conditions are absent. | Effective consent satisfying clauses 11.2–11.3, without unacceptable conditions or adverse contract changes. | **Make compliant consent and satisfaction of its conditions a Buyer-waivable completion condition**, supported by evidence and termination rights at the long-stop date; approximately 30% of revenue is exposed. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Debt repayment and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion, with correct price treatment. | **Require an agreed payout letter, direct repayment through completion funds flow and effective completion releases**; post-completion discharge leaves Buyer exposed and conflicts with the debt-free basis. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-cost treatment unstated. | Seller-funded bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with no double counting. | **Quantify and expressly allocate these amounts to Seller through the price adjustment/funds flow, backed by an indemnity for unpaid amounts**; Buyer should not inherit an unpriced transaction-triggered liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the specific SOW3 payment; **AUD 180,000** recorded open, without payment receipt or confirmatory assignment. | Verified payment and effective ownership of relevant IP, plus cover for the consequences of any title gap. | **Require payment evidence and an effective assignment at Completion; broaden the indemnity beyond the invoice to resulting claims, losses and remediation costs**; paying the fee alone may not resolve all ownership defects or consequences. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Preliminary operational matter, not expected to be material; access, scope and notification requirements remain uncertain. | Prompt evidence-based investigation, containment, legal assessment and allocation of pre-completion incident risk. | **Require investigation updates and remediation covenants plus a specific indemnity for resulting liabilities and reasonable response costs**, including regulatory amounts only where lawfully indemnifiable; uncertainty is not proof of either a confirmed breach or immateriality. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three **AUD 110,000** renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assessment of aggregate commitment, timing, cancellation rights, accruals and ordinary-course status. | **Review the AUD 330,000 package together and apply consent, price adjustment or specific protection where justified—not automatic debt treatment**; the available facts do not establish either ordinary-course treatment or a deductible liability. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations and exclusive-remedy/non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims unless expressly excepted. | Clearly distinct regimes for general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, payment obligations and covenant breaches. | **Insert an express category matrix and overriding carve-outs across every relevant clause**; otherwise general wording could silently defeat negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | Relies on DD-012’s share register showing Seller holds 100%. | Independent confirmation of all issued shares, ownership, encumbrances, options and transfer restrictions. | **Reconcile the register with corporate and issuance records, inspect relevant security arrangements and require valid completion transfer documents and title warranties**; the register alone does not establish clean, transferable ownership. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP warranties treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity and tailored IP protections, informed by diligence. | **Reopen both: seek tax protection through the applicable assessment/recovery periods plus a buffer, and longer IP survival with a higher/separate cap and targeted indemnities**; an 18-month, 20% general regime inadequately addresses latent tax and core-IP risks. |

**Priority completion protections:** Bluefen’s effective consent, Riverlark repayment/releases, Ironquay ownership resolution and a reconciled funds flow including Seller-funded bonuses. These should not be replaced merely by post-completion warranty claims.
=== END ADVICE ===
